evals.prompt: Run the research loop: why did our trial-to-paid conversion drop from 14% to 9% in September? I've put the sources in sources/ (a product analytics export, the September release notes, 12 sales call notes, and a competitor's pricing page). The growth lead decides by 1 November whether to roll back the new onboarding flow.
assertions: Runs research-plan first and writes, before synthesising, what finding would change the roll-back decision
States the stopping rule before reading the sources
The synthesis cites every claim to a listed source and location
The comparison includes a measurement hypothesis (tracking or definition change) alongside the onboarding flow and the competitor's pricing
Every evidence row in the matrix cites a listed source or is marked [assumption]
Ends with a G7 verdict from PROCEED, PROCEED WITH CONDITIONS, REVISE, RECONSIDER or BLOCKED, and the reasons for it
The reply leads with the explanation the evidence favours and what it means for the roll-back, not with the matrix

evals.prompt: Continuing the research loop. The comparison left H1 (the new onboarding flow) and H3 (the competitor's price cut on 4 September) tied, and named as discriminating: conversion for trials that started before the onboarding release on 11 September. I've added that cohort export as sources/cohorts.csv.
assertions: Treats the tie as G7 REVISE and returns to synthesise, not to plan
Adds the cohort export as a new numbered source and re-synthesises with it cited
Re-runs the comparison with the new evidence row rated across every hypothesis
Counts this as round 2 under the cap of 3
Does not add further sources that both H1 and H3 predict equally

evals.prompt: Run the research loop on why remote work is good. Non-interactive, no follow-up questions.
assertions: Emits BLOCKED: need the decision this research informs, who makes it, and by when
Does not run source-synthesis or hypothesis-comparison
Does not invent a decision or gather sources
Says in plain words what it will produce once it has the decision
